newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel chief worried by political crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel chief worried by political crisis.

text.p: Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel warned on Monday that the political crisis now enveloping Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government could have a negative impact on the economy.
"There is no doubt that from an economic point of view uncertainty is bad. Even if it comes from the political sphere, it is not positive," Frenkel told Israel Radio.

Frenkel made the remarks as concerns grew that a high-level corruption probe could make it difficult for the government to pursue economic policy matters, most critically reducing the budget deficit, or move forward with the peace process.

Some analysts expressed surprise that the Bank of Israel was willing to lower interest rates, as it announced today, because the crisis would make budget-cutting difficult. The central bank said it was lowering rates by 0.3 percentage point to 13.9 percent effective Thursday.

Netanyahu and other officials in his government are being questioned by police in connection with charges that the short-lived appointment of Roni Bar-On as attorney-general was part of a deal for a plea bargain in the corruption trial of Aryeh Deri, a key figure in the governing coalition.
Last week the prime minister was cautioned by police that statements he made to them could be used against him in court, a procedure used by police when they believe charges may be filed.
"Those who are responsible for economic policy have to display stability, display continuity and display moderation with no dramatic steps and unnecessary drama," Frenkel said.

He stressed the need to keep to policy targets, stressing the two basic goals for 1997 of meeting the inflation target of seven to 10 percent and keeping the budget deficit to less than 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
